t: In front of you is the statue of Rowland Hill, the man usually credited with the ideas behind the modern postal service. He campaigned for a Uniform Penny Post, with letters paid for in advance, which made sending them safe, quick and cheap. He is also credited with inventing the postage stamp. The statue was made by Edward Onslow Ford, an English sculptor who was known for refined portrait busts and public monuments, and who became a leading figure in the New Sculpture movement that grew up in Britain from around 1880.
